name: Orphan of the Fracture
description: The day the sky shattered, you lost everything. Family, home, certainty. You survived by luck and stubbornness, and you've carried both with you ever since.
flavor_text: Loss taught you what mattered. Survival taught you how to keep it.
narrative: You don't remember much of before. The Fracture took that, along with everything else. What you have is after — the scrambling, the hiding, the slowly building something from nothing. You learned early that the System doesn't care about your history. Only your potential.

name: Former Guild Member
description: You had a place in a guild before all this. Connections. A rank. Then something happened — a falling out, a betrayal, or just the slow erosion of believing in something that stopped believing in you.
flavor_text: The guild gave you skills. Leaving taught you to use them for yourself.
narrative: Guild life had its rhythms — the roster calls, the shared meals, the hierarchy. You miss some of it. You don't miss what made you leave. You carry the training and the wariness in equal measure.

name: Scholar's Apprentice
description: You spent years in service to someone who understood more about the System than anyone should. Some of that understanding rubbed off. A little. You're still figuring out how much.
flavor_text: Knowledge is the only armor that gets stronger the more you use it.
narrative: Your master died before answering the questions that mattered most. You have the notes, you have the methodology, and you have a growing suspicion that the answers are somewhere in the System itself — if you survive long enough to find them.

name: Street Thief
description: You took what you needed because need doesn't negotiate. You learned the city's rhythms — the guards' rotations, the merchants' patterns, the gaps between where eyes were and where they weren't.
flavor_text: Every locked door is just a question you haven't answered yet.
narrative: Theft was never the goal. Eating was the goal. Staying warm was the goal. The theft was just the method. The System gave you a classification and a fresh start, which is more than the city ever offered. You haven't decided yet whether to trust it.

name: Former Soldier
description: You served. You followed orders. You watched things happen that orders couldn't justify. Then one day you stopped following orders, and you've been figuring out what comes next ever since.
flavor_text: Discipline without purpose is just another cage.
narrative: War teaches efficiency. You strip away everything that isn't survival, everything that isn't mission, until you're not entirely sure what's left. You're carrying a weapon and a set of skills and a lot of questions about what to do with them now that the war is over.

name: Farmer's Child
description: You know what it is to work until your hands bleed and still not have enough. The Fracture took the harvest; the System took the certainty of the next one. You're here because staying wasn't viable.
flavor_text: Hard work and stubbornness can substitute for talent longer than you'd think.
narrative: The land doesn't lie to you. You always knew when rain was coming, when the soil was wrong, when an animal was sick. That kind of attention — paying careful notice to the world around you — turns out to be useful in a dungeon too.

name: Merchant's Ward
description: You grew up knowing the price of everything. Numbers, negotiation, value — you learned them before you learned to read. The System is just another market, as far as you can tell. Everything has a cost. The trick is knowing what you're willing to pay.
flavor_text: Every transaction is a negotiation. Know your leverage.
narrative: Your guardian treated you well and taught you everything — including the lesson they didn't intend: that people who understand commerce rarely do it for love of the craft. You left with gold in your pocket and a clear eye for when you're being sold something.

name: Noble's Bastard
description: You grew up between two worlds: close enough to power to understand it, too illegitimate to inherit it. You learned what privilege looks like from the outside and how to move through rooms where you technically didn't belong.
flavor_text: Neither fully in nor fully out. The best view of both sides.
narrative: Your parent never claimed you publicly. You never forgot that. You learned their world anyway — the protocols, the debts, the careful games of faction and favour — and then you left on your own terms. You have a name that opens some doors and a face that closes others.
